sources.citation: He et al., Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition, CVPR 2016
sources.passage: Increasing the depth of a conventional convolutional network can produce a degradation problem: training error can become higher even when extra layers should in principle be able to implement identity mappings. Residual networks address this optimization problem by asking a stack of layers to learn a residual function F(x) relative to its input x. An identity shortcut then adds x to the learned residual, giving the block output F(x) + x. The shortcut introduces neither additional parameters nor computational cost when dimensions match. Projection shortcuts can be used when dimensions change. This parameterization makes identity mappings easier to represent and enabled substantially deeper networks to be optimized successfully.
sources.technical_summary: ResNet addresses degradation by parameterizing a block as F(x) + x rather than directly learning H(x). Parameter-free identity shortcuts make identity mappings easy to represent, while learned projections handle dimension changes, improving optimization of substantially deeper CNNs.
sources.accessible_summary: ResNet makes very deep image-recognition networks easier to train by giving information a shortcut around groups of layers. A block learns only the needed change and adds it to its input, while adjusted shortcuts handle differently sized representations.

sources.citation: Vaswani et al., Attention Is All You Need, NeurIPS 2017
sources.passage: The Transformer is an encoder-decoder architecture for sequence transduction that replaces recurrence and convolution with attention mechanisms. Each encoder layer combines multi-head self-attention with a position-wise feed-forward network. Decoder layers additionally attend to encoder outputs and mask future positions during self-attention. Because the architecture has no recurrence, positional information is added to token representations. Scaled dot-product attention computes similarities between queries and keys, applies a softmax, and uses the resulting weights to combine values. Multiple heads perform this operation in different learned representation subspaces. Removing sequential recurrence permits substantially more parallel computation during training.
sources.technical_summary: The Transformer replaces recurrence and convolution with multi-head self-attention and position-wise feed-forward layers. Scaled dot-product attention mixes learned values using query-key similarities; positional encodings supply order, and causal masking prevents decoder access to future tokens.
sources.accessible_summary: The Transformer processes a sequence by letting each token decide which other tokens are relevant instead of reading them strictly one at a time. It tracks order separately and hides future words during generation, enabling more parallel training.
